subject: Embargoed outreach: Redwood Inference “Latency per dollar” benchmark report (embargo Feb 25)
body:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@northshorepr.com>, Kara Winters <kara@techwire.com>, Mateo Ruiz <mruiz@theinferencebrief.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Embargoed: Redwood Inference “Latency per dollar” benchmark report (embargo Feb 25)

Hi Asha, Kara, Mateo —

We’re preparing a public benchmark report focused on production economics: *latency per dollar* (plus throughput/cost) across popular open models and multiple cloud regions.

I’m sharing an embargoed draft for background + early feedback. If you’d like, we can also do a 20–30 min briefing under embargo.

Proposed embargo:
- Embargo lifts: Tue, Feb 25, 2025 @ 6:00am PT / 9:00am ET
- Publication window: Feb 25 (we’ll coordinate exact timing with you)

Angles we think will resonate:
1) “Serving is the new moat”: operational + economic reality vs raw model capability
2) Why region-by-region data changes vendor selection (and how teams should evaluate)
3) A reproducible methodology that engineers can sanity-check (no black box claims)

Notes / guardrails:
- We’ll publish methodology + constraints prominently.
- We are not positioning this as an ‘absolute fastest’ claim; results include variance language and confidence guidance.

Attachments (embargoed):
- RedwoodInfe_BenchmarkReport_Embargoed_v0.9.pdf
- RedwoodInfe_PressKit_Embargoed.zip (boilerplate, logos, key stats, etc.)
- LatencyPerDollar_MethodologyFAQ_v0.9.pdf
- RedwoodInfe_ChartsPreview_Embargoed.png

If you’re open to a briefing, please reply with 2–3 time windows between Feb 18–21.

Thanks,
Camila

Camila Reyes
VP Marketing, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0184

Subject: Re: Embargoed: Redwood Inference “Latency per dollar” benchmark report (embargo Feb 25)

Camila — received, thank you.

A few notes + questions so we can tighten the pitch:

1) Embargo timing: 6am PT works; can we also specify “no coverage before 9am ET” for east coast outlets? (Some editors prefer ET.)

2) Pitch angle options (recommended subject lines):
- “Latency per dollar: a new benchmark for LLM inference economics (multi-region)”
- “Serving performance varies by region more than teams expect — here’s the data”
- “Redwood publishes reproducible LLM inference economics benchmark”

3) Quotes: can we request two exec quotes (Marketing + Applied ML/Methodology sponsor) and one customer/prospect “why we care about latency/$” quote? Even if anonymous.

4) Attachments: press kit ZIP is great. For select press, I suggest a separate 1-page “Key findings” PDF (easier for editors).

I’ll send a draft outreach list + email copy EOD if that works.

Asha

Asha Patel
Northshore PR (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

+1 on calling out ET explicitly. Field teams are already planning Feb 25 follow-ups and “9am ET” will reduce confusion.

One more suggestion for press/analyst angle:
- Procurement POV: “Cost per token isn’t enough; you need latency/$ and reliability constraints to compare offers.”

Also, we should be careful that outreach copy doesn’t imply:
- “best” or “#1” broadly
- “apples-to-apples across every vendor” (we should anchor to what we actually measured + constraints)

If you want a third quote, I can provide a sales POV on how teams evaluate inference vendors (and why economics matter in production).

Jordan

From: Kara Winters <kara@techwire.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 1:48 PM PT
Subject: Re: Embargoed: Redwood Inference “Latency per dollar” benchmark report (embargo Feb 25)

Hi Camila — thanks for sending. Confirming we can accept the embargo (Feb 25 @ 9am ET).

A couple clarifying questions before I commit to a briefing:

1) How are you defining “latency per dollar”? Is it p50, p95, or something else? Are you including infrastructure costs, or just your API pricing?

2) Will the report compare against other hosted providers, or is this strictly Redwood’s regions + configs?

3) Can you share what models/families are included (even a short list) so I can gauge relevance for our readers?

If you have 20 minutes on Feb 19 or Feb 20 afternoon ET, I can do a quick call.

Best,
Kara

Kara Winters
Senior Reporter, TechWire

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kara Winters <kara@techwire.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@northshorepr.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 2:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Embargoed: Redwood Inference “Latency per dollar” benchmark report (embargo Feb 25)

Kara — confirmed, thank you.

Quick answers inline:

1) Definition: we report p50 and p95 latency (end-to-end request latency for the defined workloads) and compute “latency per dollar” as a derived metric using measured latency + our metered cost for the same run. We call out the exact formula and units in the methodology appendix. We also publish throughput and cost per 1M tokens alongside it so readers can sanity-check.

2) Comparisons: the main table is Redwood-run across regions with a single harness/config for consistency. We’re careful not to make blanket “provider X vs provider Y” claims because apples-to-apples requires identical workloads, regions, and pricing assumptions. We do include guidance on how teams can reproduce the methodology for their own evaluation.

3) Model coverage: it’s a curated set of popular open model families used in production today (chat + embeddings baseline). I’m keeping specifics in the embargoed report, but happy to walk through on the call and we can also share the list in writing under embargo.

Re: briefing — I can do:
- Wed Feb 19: 1:30–3:00pm ET
- Thu Feb 20: 2:00–4:00pm ET

If you pick a slot, Asha can send a calendar hold.

Camila

From: Mateo Ruiz <mruiz@theinferencebrief.com>

Cc: Asha Patel <asha@northshorepr.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 9:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: Embargoed: Redwood Inference “Latency per dollar” benchmark report (embargo Feb 25)

Camila — appreciate the draft.

Two asks:

1) Can you share 2–3 charts (high-res) that are representative? The PNG preview is helpful but not publishable.

2) I’d like to talk to whoever owns the methodology (Applied ML / perf). Specifically, I want to understand what you did about caching/batching and how you avoided tuning purely for the benchmark.

Also, will you name competitor offerings in the report? If not, I’m going to need a clear explanation in the story so readers understand what the data is (and isn’t).

I’m available Feb 18 morning PT or Feb 21 mid-day PT.

Thanks,
Mateo

Mateo Ruiz
Editor, The Inference Brief

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Ruiz <mruiz@theinferencebrief.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@northshorepr.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Embargoed: Redwood Inference “Latency per dollar” benchmark report (embargo Feb 25)

Mateo — yes on both.

1) High-res charts: we can share a small set of embargoed, publication-ready charts. Asha will send a link to a press-only folder (same embargo terms) with:
- 3x charts (SVG + PNG)
- a “key findings” one-pager
- boilerplate + logo pack

2) Methodology owner: we can bring our methodology sponsor (Jonas Weber, Applied ML / Performance & Evals) into the briefing to go deep on caching/batching policy, warmups, variance/reruns, and how we keep runs representative of production usage.

On competitor naming: the report is explicit about what we measured and why we’re cautious about direct cross-provider comparisons without shared harness + region + cost assumptions. We’re happy to provide a clear paragraph you can quote that explains the constraint (and why reproducibility matters more than a one-off “winner” claim).

Availability:
- Tue Feb 18: 9:00–10:30am PT works (preferred)
- Fri Feb 21: 11:30am–1:00pm PT also works

Let me know what you prefer and we’ll lock it.

Camila

Camila Reyes
VP Marketing, Redwood Inference

(Embargo reminder: Feb 25, 2025 @ 6:00am PT / 9:00am ET)
